title: OS Grid Reference Distance Calculator
description: Measure straight-line distance between two OS grid references with the OS Grid Reference Distance Calculator — eastings and northings, exactly. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, TQ 300 800 to TQ 330 840 is exactly 5.00 km — a 3-4-5 triangle hiding inside London's grid: 3 km east, 4 km north, 5 km between the points.
quick_answer: The OS Grid Reference Distance Calculator measures the straight-line distance between two Ordnance Survey grid references by converting them to eastings and northings and applying Pythagoras. Enter both references and read the distance in metres, kilometres or miles — the grid's own flat geometry, exact within the references' precision.

TQ 300 800 → easting 530,000, northing 180,000. TQ 330 840 → 533,000 and 184,000. Differences: 3,000 m east, 4,000 m north; distance = √(3,000² + 4,000²) = 5,000 m exactly.

Two 6-figure references locate their points within 100 m squares, so their distance carries up to ~140 m of inherited fuzz. Ten-figure references (1 m squares) make the same calculation survey-crisp. The distance cannot be better than the references.

What datum sits under the grid?
OSGB36. GPS lat/lon (WGS84) for the same ground can sit up to roughly a hundred metres away from the grid's reading — the BNG helper explains the shift.
